text: Stocks closed sharply higher in Friday's shortened session: the Nasdaq rose 2.3% and the S&P 500 1.6%, capping their best week in over a year. QQQ ended at $650.99, TQQQ up 7.9% and SQQQ down 7.7%.
Gold held its rebound into the close, ending near $3,653, up $87.50, for its first weekly gain in three weeks.
Silver finished near $43.62, up about 5.3%, and the gold/silver ratio fell to about 83.8 from 86.1. SLV closed up 6.2% at $39.40 and AGQ about 12% at $32.79.
Gold miners surged: GDX closed up 7.2% at $79.18 and GDXJ up 8.2% at $94.82.
Treasury yields rose across the board as money moved out of safe assets: the 10-year closed at 4.94% (+9 bp) and the 2-year at 4.69% (+8 bp).
Brent gave back an early climb to $98 and settled at $95.44, down 1.2% on the day but up about 3% on the week, ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting.
The VIX closed at 23.81, back below 25, and the yen ended near 159.5 per dollar.
